title: Multiplying the last elements of H1-regular tuples
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $s\geq0$, and let $h_1,\ldots,h_s,f,g\in R$. Use the Koszul complex and homology of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. If $H_1(K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s,f))=0$ and $H_1(K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s,g))=0$, then $H_1(K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s,fg))=0$. The prefix may be empty, and no locality, Noetherian, nonzero-ring or proper-ideal assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular, clause (1), specialized to M=R.

proof.text: For any complex $P$, identify $P\otimes_RR$ with $P$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Bilinearity gives $(ax)\otimes1=x\otimes a$; linearity of the differential gives $d(ax)=a\,d(x)$, so these inverse maps identify cycles, boundaries and their quotients. Thus the two assumed vanishing statements hold equally for the complexes tensored with $R$.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular (1); explicit cycle chase using Tags 0628/0629, lemma-cone-koszul-abstract and lemma-cone-koszul.

proof.text: Put $A=K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\otimes_RR$ and $B_t=K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s,t)\otimes_RR$. Apply the cited coordinate lemma with $M=R$ separately for $t=f,g,fg$. It identifies $(B_t)_0$ with $A_0$, $(B_t)_1$ with $A_1\oplus A_0$, and $(B_t)_2$ with $A_2\oplus A_1$, with differentials $D_{t,1}(x,y)=d_1x+ty$ and $D_{t,2}(u,v)=(d_2u+tv,-d_1v)$. We use these coordinates below, writing $d$ for the appropriately typed differential of $A$.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular (1); explicit cycle chase using Tags 0628/0629, lemma-cone-koszul-abstract and lemma-cone-koszul.

proof.text: Take any cycle $(x,y)\in(B_{fg})_1$, so $dx+fg\,y=0$. The pair $(x,fy)\in(B_g)_1$ is a cycle since $dx+g(fy)=0$. By $H_1(B_g)=0$ and the definition $H_1=\ker D_1/\operatorname{im}D_2$, choose $u\in A_2$, $v\in A_1$ with $x=du+gv$ and $fy=-dv$.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular (1); explicit cycle chase using Tags 0628/0629, lemma-cone-koszul-abstract and lemma-cone-koszul.

proof.text: The pair $(v,y)\in(B_f)_1$ is now a cycle, since $dv+fy=0$. The other hypothesis $H_1(B_f)=0$ gives $w\in A_2$, $q\in A_1$ with $v=dw+fq$ and $y=-dq$.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular (1); explicit cycle chase using Tags 0628/0629, lemma-cone-koszul-abstract and lemma-cone-koszul.

proof.text: Linearity and commutativity give $x=du+g(dw+fq)=d(u+gw)+fg\,q$ and $y=-dq$. Consequently $(x,y)=D_{fg,2}(u+gw,q)$ is a boundary. Every cycle is a boundary, hence $H_1(B_{fg})=0$. The identification in step 1 gives $H_1(K_R(h_1,\ldots,h_s,fg))=0$. All formulas also hold for $s=0$, when $A_1=A_2=0$, and for the zero ring; no cancellation or properness assumption was used.

source.place: Tag 062G, lemma-mult-koszul-regular (1); explicit cycle chase using Tags 0628/0629, lemma-cone-koszul-abstract and lemma-cone-koszul.
